notes: Transcript edits normalize technical terms and symbols using the slide and surrounding utterance. Ambiguous algebra is not reconstructed as a quotation.
36, 78–83: use Θ for temperature, F in newtons and pressure in N/m². The five-variable example has dimension rank 3, hence exactly two independent groups.
103–107: the length balance includes +1 from F; read a = b = −2 and c = −1. The normalization on the slide is F/(ρV²L²).
133–134, 217–221: the wave is a surface gravity wave. The Froude speed convention is V/√(gL). T in the model-time ratio denotes time, not temperature.
154–157: Ma = V/a; the force ratio is Ma². 172–179: use t* = tV/L. Eu is the Euler number, not the Eckert number.
205–206: constant length and time ratios give a constant velocity ratio; their numerical values need not be equal.
234–239: the third extra variable is pipe length L. Reynolds number uses D; the on-screen notes amend those symbols.

248: the ASR reads 1.155; the displayed fit reads 0.155. Use the displayed coefficient in the study note. The first-row table on p.33 and the worked substitution on p.35 give different pressure drops.
